description: Declared mutants of the camera Module and of MakeOrthographic (docs/architecture/target/v2/transform-camera-declaration.zh-Hant.md, section 6.3; Design Invariants CM-1 to CM-5 in docs/architecture/target/v2/camera.zh-Hant.md; ids cm- and math-). A mutant is killed only when the named test case fails with the expected message.

mutants.what: Camera2d's initial Projection is the perspective one
Default2d keeps near -1000, far 1000 (a smaller z in front) instead of the user's choice (b): near and far swapped
mutants.expect: \[cm\-camera2d\-ortho\] near and far are not swapped

mutants.what: a camera without a target size is valid
the perspective aspect is height over width
UpdateCameras writes ComputedCamera every frame: Changed<ComputedCamera> holds when nothing changed
WindowSize uses the physical size instead of the logical one
mutants.find:
const float logicalWidth = static_cast<float>(viewport.size.x) / size->scaleFactor;
    const float logicalHeight = static_cast<float>(viewport.size.y) / size->scaleFactor;
mutants.replace:
const float logicalWidth = static_cast<float>(viewport.size.x);
    const float logicalHeight = static_cast<float>(viewport.size.y);

mutants.what: the orthographic area is always centred, whatever viewportOrigin says
mutants.find:
const float originX = width * orthographic.viewportOrigin.x;
    const float originY = height * orthographic.viewportOrigin.y;
mutants.replace:
const float originX = width * 0.5F;
    const float originY = height * 0.5F;

mutants.what: the orthographic projection ignores scale
mutants.find:
return Math::MakeOrthographic(orthographic.scale * -originX, orthographic.scale * (width - originX),
                                  orthographic.scale * -originY, orthographic.scale * (height - originY),
mutants.replace:
return Math::MakeOrthographic(-originX, width - originX,
                                  -originY, height - originY,

mutants.replace:

mutants.what: the camera's viewport is ignored: the aspect comes from the whole target
the viewport is not clamped into the target
mutants.find:
ClampAxis(viewport.position.x, viewport.size.x, size->physicalSize.x);
    ClampAxis(viewport.position.y, viewport.size.y, size->physicalSize.y);

mutants.what: ViewportToWorld takes Bevy's reversed depth: the ray starts at the far plane
a viewport position goes to NDC without flipping y (viewport +Y is down, NDC +Y is up)
the conversions take the position inside the viewport, not the target's (Bevy subtracts the viewport's corner)
mutants.find:
const float x = (position.x - rect.minimum.x) / rect.size.x * 2.0F - 1.0F;
    const float y = (position.y - rect.minimum.y) / rect.size.y * 2.0F - 1.0F;
mutants.replace:
const float x = position.x / rect.size.x * 2.0F - 1.0F;
    const float y = position.y / rect.size.y * 2.0F - 1.0F;

mutants.what: a depth below 0 is reported past the far plane (Bevy's reversed reading)
ComputedCamera's hash writes valid: a derived value changes the summary
mutants.replace: inline void HashValue(Kernel::Hasher& h, const ComputedCamera& v) { Kernel::HashValue(h, v.valid); }

mutants.what: CameraTargetSizes' hash writes whether target 0 has a size: a machine's window size changes the summary
mutants.replace: inline void HashValue(Kernel::Hasher& h, const CameraTargetSizes& v) { Kernel::HashValue(h, v.Find(CameraTarget{}) != nullptr); }

mutants.what: MakeOrthographic maps nearClip to depth 1 and farClip to 0 (the reversed depth of Bevy) instead of the math.md clip convention
Camera does not bring CameraTarget: a Camera2d entity has no target and UpdateCameras skips it
CameraOptions is not read: a World with the skeleton off cannot name where UpdateCameras runs
mutants.find: const CameraOptions options = given != nullptr ? *given : CameraOptions{};
mutants.cases: camera: a World with the skeleton off*

mutants.what: Neither UpdateCameras nor UpdateCameraViews is put in the public set CameraUpdate: a System ordered after the set runs before the update. The set is then empty and the kernel reports the reader's order as D-E4 at startup; the case tags that failure too (since A1 both camera Systems are in the set, and one alone left out is still ordered before the set's readers through the other, so the mutant takes both out)
mutants.cases: camera: a System ordered after CameraUpdate*

mutants.what: a second Set of one id keeps the old size (a resized window is never seen)
Remove leaves the size
Find returns the next larger id's size for an id that was never set
mutants.find: return at != sizes_.end() && at->first == target.id ? &at->second : nullptr;
